definition: Predicting the bounding box of the object in an image, usually alongside its class.
details: Predicting the bounding box of the object in an image, usually alongside its class. It is the localization component of detection and weakly supervised approaches use class activation maps.

explainer.lead: Object localization predicts the bounding box of an object in an image, usually together with its class. It matters because it is the localization component of detection.

tiers.eli5: It points at where the thing is in the picture by drawing a box around it, rather than only saying what it is.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers regress box coordinates from image features; a common pitfall is that weakly supervised versions rely on class activation maps, which give coarse localization.
tiers.paperLevel: Output the coordinates of a bounding box around the object, optionally with its class; weakly supervised approaches use class activation maps, whose localization is coarse.

explainer.example: For a photo of a cat, the model returns the box coordinates around the cat and the label 'cat'.
